To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the chemoselectivity of Sonogashira crosscoupling reactions of 2,6-dihalopyridines is dependent on the substitution pattern of the starting materials and that 3,5-di- and 3,5,2,6-tetrabromopyridines can be used as starting materials to obtain mono- and dialkynylpyridine derivatives.
3,5- dibromo-2, 6-dichloro pyridine can be employed as a new substrate for Sonogashira cross- coupling reaction.
3,5- dibromo-2, 6-dichloro- pyridine is an interesting substrate for the chemosele ctive synthesis of a variety of mono- di- tri- and tetralkynylated products.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new, efficient, and versatile method for the chemodivergent synthesis of mono-, di- and trialkynylated derivatives of 2,6-dihalopyridines.
the development of new synthetic strategies to obtain alkynylated heterocycles in a chemoselective and regioselective way.
the development of a new method for the synthesis of alkynated pyridines from 2,3-dibromo-5,6-dicholoropyridine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

3,5- dibromo-2, 6-dichloro pyridine and its derivatives are superior substrates for Sonogashira cross coupling reactions as compared to 2,3-dichloro-6-bromo pyridine, and that the latter is a better substrate for Sonogashiratype reactions.
3,5- dibromo-2, 6- dichloropyridine is a more versatile substrate for Sonogashira cross- coupling reactions than 2,3,5,6- tetrachloropyri dine.
3,5-bromo-2,5-dichloropyrimidine is an excellent starting material for the preparation of mono- and di-alkynylated 2,5-dibromopyrimidines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Sonogashira cross coupling reactions of 3-bromo-2,5-dichloropyidines and 3,5-bromo-2-chloropyridines give access to monoalkynylpyridine and di-alkynylpyidines respectively, while 3,5- dichloro-2-bromopyridine gives the di-alkynpyridines.
we have found a way to selectively synthesize mono-, di-, and trialkynylated 2,6-dihalopyridines.
3,5-disubstituted pyridines are more reactive towards the Sonogashira cross coupling reactions than 2,5-disubtituted pyridines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chemoselectivity of Sonogashira coupling reactions of 3-bromo-2,5-dichloropyrimidine and 3-bromo-pyrimidine can be controlled by the choice of the halide leaving group.
the regioselectivity of the Sonogashira coupling of 2,6-dihalopyridines is highly dependent on the nature of the halogens present at the pyridine ring.
2,3-dichloropyrimidines and 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)-2,6-dihalopyridines can be used as a source of the halogen atoms in the cross-coupling of 3,4,5,6- tetrahalopyridines.
